record.original_question: Does there exist an infinite square-free word w such that w = w ▷β w for some infinite β?

evidence.quote: Does there exist an infinite square-free word w such that w = w β w for some infinite β? 

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet and let $\Sigma^\omega$ denote the set of (right-)infinite words over $\Sigma$. An infinite word $w \in \Sigma^\omega$ is called square-free if there is no nonempty finite word $u$ such that $uu$ occurs as a factor (contiguous block) of $w$.

Given two infinite words $u, v \in \Sigma^\omega$ and an infinite binary word $\beta \in \{0,1\}^\omega$ in which both letters $0$ and $1$ occur infinitely often, the shuffle of $u$ and $v$ directed by $\beta$, denoted $u \triangleright_\beta v$, is the unique infinite word obtained by reading, for $n = 1, 2, 3, \ldots$, the next unread letter of $u$ when the $n$-th letter of $\beta$ is $0$, and the next unread letter of $v$ when the $n$-th letter of $\beta$ is $1$.

An infinite word $w$ is said to be self-shuffling if there exists an infinite binary word $\beta$ (with both $0$ and $1$ appearing infinitely often) such that
$$w \;=\; w \triangleright_\beta w.$$

Question: Does there exist an infinite word $w$ over some finite alphabet which is simultaneously square-free and self-shuffling?
artifact.status_search_result: The question was answered affirmatively by Charlier, Kamae, Puzynina, and Zamboni (2014, arXiv:1401.6536, "Infinite square-free self-shuffling words"), who construct an infinite square-free word $w$ over a 3-letter alphabet that is self-shuffling, resolving Harju's question. The result also appeared in The Electronic Journal of Combinatorics 22(1) #P55 (2015).

status_evidence.title: Infinite square-free self-shuffling words
status_evidence.claim: Existence of an infinite square-free self-shuffling word is proved.

status_evidence.title: On Shuffling of Infinite Square-Free Words
status_evidence.snippet: On shuffling of infinite square-free words, Electron. J. Combin. 22(1) #P55, 2015.
status_evidence.claim: Published affirmative answer to the self-shuffling square-free question.
